wu: Mime the action: Students take turns miming an action (e.g., eating, studying, playing football) while others guess using 'He/She was ...-ing'. Teacher writes guesses on the board.
wuAlt: Chain reaction: Student 1 mimes an action, Student 2 adds another, forming a story chain using 'and then he was ...-ing'
Find someone who: Students walk around asking 'Were you ...-ing last night?' and find classmates who say yes.
pres: Show a 4-picture comic strip of a boy at the park. Point to each picture and model: 'He was playing football. He was eating ice cream. He was sitting on a bench. He was watching birds.' Elicit more examples from students using the pictures.
presAlt: Use realia: Hold up a toy car and a toy person; move them to show actions while saying 'He was driving the car'
Draw a simple scene on the board with 3-4 characters doing different things and label with past continuous sentences.
prac: While-clause chains: In pairs, Student 1 starts with 'While I was walking to school, I saw ...', Student 2 continues with 'While he was seeing ..., he heard ...', and so on. Teacher provides sentence starters on the board.
pracAlt: Picture match: Give students 6 action cards and 6 location cards; they make sentences like 'She was swimming at the beach'
Fill-in-the-blank worksheet with 10 past continuous sentences to complete.
ls: Listen to a short story about a rainy day. Students listen and draw 3 things the family was doing (e.g., 'Dad was cooking', 'Mum was reading', 'Sister was painting'). Check drawings as a class.
re: Action relay: Two lines of students race to the board to write a past continuous sentence about a teacher's mimes (e.g., 'Teacher was clapping'). First team to write 3 correct sentences wins.
prod: Group story: Each group gets 6 picture cards showing a sequence of actions (e.g., getting ready for school). They write 6 sentences using past continuous to tell the story, then present it to the class.
rw: Read 'The Hare and the Tortoise' fable. Students underline all past continuous verbs (e.g., 'was running', 'was sleeping'). Then, in pairs, they write 2 new sentences about what another animal was doing during the race.
st: Read a simplified version of 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf' with student volunteers acting out the past continuous actions (e.g., one student pretends to be the boy 'was shouting', another pretends to be a villager 'was running'). End with: 'Today we learned to talk about actions in the past using was/were + -ing. Great job, everyone! Thank you for your hard work.'
g: Students act out past continuous actions (e.g., 'was sleeping') for teammates to guess
Teams race to write past continuous sentences about pictures shown on the projector
Teacher writes sentences with errors (e.g., 'He was play football'); students correct them
Each student adds one past continuous sentence to continue a class story
Teacher shows a picture, students say 3 things people were doing in it
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 4-sentence story about what their family was doing last night
Support: Use sentence frames like 'He/She was ________ing at ________' to write their story
hw: Option 1: Draw 6 pictures of what you were doing at different times yesterday and write a sentence under each
Option 2: Write 6 sentences about what a character from your favorite cartoon was doing last weekend
Option 3: Interview a family member about what they were doing at 3 specific times yesterday and write down their answers
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references like 'While I was eating couscous, my friend was playing football' to make the grammar more relatable and memorable for local learners.
